name: arch-evolve
thesis: Forge's layer boundary is already in the right place; what is missing is not a framework but a render discipline and a headless facade. Keep createElement plus CSSOM, keep compose(), and add exactly two things: a ForgeCore facade that takes the ten blocks of domain logic out of ui/app.mjs, and a ~150-line view kernel that gives every screen a pure (view-model) => Element signature with keyed patching and one async landing point. Then grow screens one vertical slice at a time, each leaving Forge usable and each rolling back to a pinned loader. This is the only option whose first phase is also the mitigation the risk register already assigns to scope creep, and it is the option the approved visual direction has already been sequenced for. Its honest cost: the markup stays hand-written, so a 25-component inventory is enforced by committed fixtures rather than by types, and the unminified bundle grows about a quarter.

layering.principle: Below forge/src/ui/ nothing moves. A_ARCHITECTURE_MAP.md A.2 already marks every storage/transport/budget/runner/reconcile module 'UI-independent: yes' and the leakage runs the other way: ui/app.mjs owns harvestEntry (:29-47), resumeBlockedReason (:159-163), blockedPaths (:166-170), loadPicker/selectManifest (:186-225), _drive (:264-300), resolveCaptures/_materialize (:323-366), exportJob (:369-406) and _persist (:408-410). Evolve = extract that, add a render kernel, keep everything else.

ui_technology.choice: No framework. Keep document.createElement via dom.mjs h() and one CSSOM stylesheet, and add a ~150-line render kernel (forge/src/ui/view.mjs) that gives screens a pure (vm, actions) => Element signature, keyed list patching, focus preservation and a single async landing point.
why_not_a_component_library: Every template-literal library (Lit, htm, uhtml, hyperHTML) ultimately writes markup through innerHTML or an equivalent HTML-string sink. forge/build.mjs fails the build on any /innerHTML/ in the bundle and forge/test/ui.test.mjs:29-34 greps the whole of src for innerHTML|outerHTML|insertAdjacentHTML|document.write. Adopting one means relaxing a shipped safety gate for a convenience; that is the wrong trade in a tool whose non-negotiables list starts with 'no innerHTML'.

A VDOM library (Preact ~11 KB gzip, plus hooks) does not use innerHTML and would pass the gate, but it buys re-render diffing that the kernel provides in 150 lines, while adding a dependency to a bundle that must be reproducible byte-for-byte from source for the release pin (the bundle-diff CI job) and self-contained for the single @require model.

JSX or any build-time template step adds a compile stage between forge/src and forge_bundle.js. Today the bundle is one esbuild IIFE with no transform, which is what makes 'a fresh build equals the checked-in bundle' a cheap CI assertion.

The honest cost of saying no: 25 WCM components (A.12) rendered by hand in h() calls are enforced by convention plus snapshots, not by a type system. That is a real maintainability debt and it is why test_architecture leans hard on committed DOM and view-model fixtures.
ui_technology.no_innerHTML_satisfaction: Unchanged and mechanically enforced: the build gate in forge/build.mjs and the static test at forge/test/ui.test.mjs:29-34 both keep passing because no new sink is introduced. The kernel only calls document.createElement, appendChild, removeChild and setAttribute through the existing h()/append()/replace() helpers (dom.mjs:3-27).
ui_technology.single_bundle_require_model: Unchanged. One esbuild IIFE, format 'iife', one @require line pinned to an immutable commit (forge_loader_user.js:12). No dynamic import(): esbuild would either inline it (no benefit) or emit a runtime fetch of a second URL that pin_release.py does not pin and that offline/evicted recovery cannot rely on. 'Lazy' therefore means deferred parse, never deferred fetch.

bundle_size_estimate.honest_cost: Evolve does not shrink the bundle; it grows the unminified artefact by about 24%. R-06 is made worse in bytes and is only paid back by (a) the minified build, which is user decision K-14, and (b) the deferred-JSON-parse change, which saves parse time and heap rather than bytes. A raw+gzip ceiling assertion becomes a CI gate so the growth is visible per phase.

ui_technology.how_screens_become_testable: A screen stops taking `app` and takes a plain view-model. That means (1) unit tests with no DOM at all over core.snapshot(); (2) jsdom tests that render one screen from a hand-built vm without composing the whole graph; (3) a deterministic DOM serializer (tag, sorted attributes, text) over .f-app producing committed fixtures under forge/test/fixtures/screens/<screen>.<state>.txt, diffed in CI exactly as the 11 tRPC envelope fixtures already are. Because h() builds real nodes with no HTML string sink, that serialization is stable.

journal_v1_to_v2.recommendation: Do not move the journal schema for phases E0-E3. The one genuinely new per-job fact is repository sync state; carry it in a SEPARATE key tnr_forge_sync_v1:<jobId> so JOURNAL_VERSION stays 1 and R-09 stays at zero for the first four slices.
journal_v1_to_v2.when_v2_is_unavoidable: If a later phase needs a field inside the journal record itself (for example a journaled Studio promotion, K-39), add MIGRATIONS[1] = (job) => ({...job, v: 2, sync: job.sync ?? {state:'unknown'}}) into the empty table at forge/src/storage/journal.mjs:407. Purely additive; no field is renamed or removed.
journal_v1_to_v2.hard_constraint: migrate() already refuses a record newer than the running bundle ('journal v2 is newer than this bundle', journal.mjs:413). Rollback is 'reinstall the previous pinned loader' (forge_loader_user.js:12), so a v2 record written by a release the operator then rolls back is UNREADABLE. Therefore v2 may only be WRITTEN one release after the release that can READ it ships and is pinned. That two-release rule is a policy decision worth the director confirming, not a detail.
journal_v1_to_v2.never: A failed migration never deletes a v1 record. It parks it under <key>.corrupt, which is the pattern compat.mjs already uses, and surfaces it through journal.broken (journal.mjs:221-228), which today has no renderer at all (A.4.1 item 5).

indexeddb.today: tnr_forge v2 with stores captures and capture_snapshots; the v1->v2 upgrade was additive and an existing v1 database keeps its captures store (captures.mjs:29-34).
indexeddb.change: Repository text (manifest bodies, subtype registry, build results) moves OUT of the captures store, where app.mjs:198-200 puts it today under the synthetic path 'github.contents'. It goes into a SEPARATE database tnr_forge_repo v1 rather than a third store in tnr_forge.
indexeddb.why_separate_db: If the repo store were added as tnr_forge v3, an operator who rolled back to the previous pinned loader would have a bundle asking for v2 against an existing v3 database, which throws VersionError on open and takes the capture cache and every full-capture snapshot with it. A separate database makes rollback clean: the old bundle simply never opens it.
indexeddb.migration_of_existing_rows: None. The existing github.contents rows are a cache keyed by GitHub blob sha; they are deleted on first read of the new store and refetched. They cost no game budget, so there is nothing to preserve.

storage_migration.retained_builder_keys: tnr_bk_idmap_v1 and tnr_bk_gh_v1 (compat.mjs:4-5) are untouched in shape and semantics for the whole roadmap. Builder v4.32 keeps reading and writing them, which is required while Builder stays installed (B.3, R-10, K-11). Any idmap export/import/reset added for gate G-06 round-trips that exact shape, proven by an export -> reset -> import byte-equality test.
storage_migration.settings: GitHub PAT and sync flag stay under tnr_bk_gh_v1 (screens.mjs:131). New per-device preferences (Reduce motion, Daylight) go in a NEW key tnr_forge_prefs_v1 rather than being folded into the shared Builder key.
storage_migration.rollback: Every phase's storage change must satisfy one rule: a record written by release N is either readable by release N-1 or explicitly refused with a message naming the version. The phase acceptance gate replays a real exported journal from harvests/inbox through migrate() as a fixture (R-09's own mitigation asks for exactly this).

release_strategy.bundles: One. One esbuild IIFE, one @require, one pinned commit (forge_loader_user.js:12). No code splitting, no second artefact, no dynamic import.
release_strategy.why_not_split: A second URL is not covered by the immutable jsDelivr pin, would need a second entry in pin_release.py TARGETS and a second line in the loader, would add a network dependency on a tool whose whole recovery story assumes the bundle is already in the browser, and would break the bundle-diff CI job's 'fresh build equals checked-in bundle' assertion for the primary artefact.

lazy_contract_data.what: fields.json, nested.json and 32b_DATA_pool.json are embedded by esbuild as top-level JavaScript object literals (forge_bundle.js:2802 b_DATA_pool_default, :6245 fields_default, :6658 nested_default). Their sources total 124,782 bytes.
lazy_contract_data.problem: The loader matches the whole game origin, so the IIFE evaluates on EVERY game page; boot() returns immediately on an unarmed tab (main.mjs:171-173) but the object literals have already been parsed by then.
lazy_contract_data.change: Switch those three imports to esbuild's text loader and JSON.parse them behind a memoised accessor called from Validator and the pool resolver. Same bytes on the wire (roughly +2% for JSON string escaping), but the parse and the retained heap move to first use, i.e. never on an INERT page.
lazy_contract_data.tier: Inferred. The claim that JSON.parse of a string beats a JS object literal, and by how much on Firefox Android, was not measured here. The embedding shape IS source-verified at the bundle lines above.

release_strategy.loader_and_pin: The two-stage pin is unchanged. Phase E0 must have main green, which requires the release_loader.test.mjs:47 'exactly one @x-release-pending marker' assertion relaxed to 'at most one'. The only existing fix lives on the ChatGPT branch at 824c4d58 bundled with unrelated rewrites (R-22, CF-19), so this option does NOT author a competing change: it records the assignment as an E0 prerequisite.
release_strategy.minification: Recommended (measured 397,984 -> 232,720 raw, 74,969 -> 52,556 gzip) but it is user decision K-14, and it must keep the bundle byte-reproducible on the pinned esbuild 0.28.2 so the CI bundle-diff stays meaningful.

recovery.principle: The view-model is DERIVED from durable sources (journal in localStorage, IndexedDB, the retained Builder keys). Nothing that matters lives only in App.state (app.mjs:58) any more, so a crash mid-render loses only a scroll position.
eviction: The only piece of App.state worth persisting is the selected manifest PATH, not the parsed plan: on resume the manifest is re-fetched and re-parsed, so a stale plan can never be run against a manifest that changed under it.

navigator.storage.persist() keeps being requested best-effort on mount (app.mjs:408-410) but the result moves into core.health so every surface renders one answer. Whether Firefox Android grants it is still Inferred (A.5).

The capture snapshots that a bundle is built from stay immutable and are never invalidated by a write (captures.mjs, A.5). Deleting them stays a separate, separately-worded, separately-confirmed action (screens.mjs:107-118).
crash_mid_run: Unchanged and deliberately so. withSent() still flushes SENT before the fetch (journal.mjs:330-335); run() still refuses a job holding SENT items and resume() reconciles first (A.7 citing runner.mjs:193,242).

The new structured job:progress event is advisory: an adversarial test asserts no progress value can produce a journal transition or advance an item state. A progress event is UI comfort; the journal is the record.

No new control anywhere is labelled Retry or Try again for a mutation class. 'Try again' exists only for retry-safe classes such as a failed GitHub listing or a cache open (D_VISUAL_SYSTEM.md departure 16).
network_loss: New sync states per RB section 11: Draft saved locally / Repository revision saved / Build requested / Building / Build result received / Repository unavailable - retry save / Build failed / Build blocked by design decision. For a results bundle the two that matter are 'synced' and 'unsynced'.

Today Github.put throws on a non-2xx and exportJob falls back to showing the bundle as text (app.mjs:402-405), and the journal records nothing (A.4.1 item 4, R-07). Under evolve the attempt is recorded with its error and a retry-on-demand action; never an automatic retry loop, because the repository automation uses rebase/retry on disjoint paths and a racing app-side retry is exactly the failure mode R-07 names.
A failed sync is a DURABLE surface, not a toast (R-25).
recovery.the_bug_this_fixes: Behaviour-proven in the UX audit and confirmed in the source this pass: showExport prepends the results card to $main (app.mjs:182), and _drive's finally block calls refresh() (app.mjs:299) which replace()s $main. With GitHub sync off, the operator's only copy of the results bundle is wiped by the very next render. Under the view-model the pending export is vm state, so a re-render re-renders it. risks: Evolve does not shrink the bundle. Unminified it grows about 24% (measured base 397,984 B raw / 74,304 B gzip; projected ~493 KB / ~103 KB), which makes R-06 worse in bytes on a phone. The only genuine byte relief is minify:true, which is user decision K-14, and the JSON-parse deferral saves parse time and heap, not bytes.

E1 is the classic silent-behaviour-change phase: 'move ten blocks, change nothing' is exactly where a wording or an ordering quietly shifts. The mitigation is mechanical (E0 commits the DOM snapshots; E1 must leave them byte-identical) but the mitigation only works if E0 actually lands first, unedited.

Keeping hand-written h() markup means the 25-component inventory in A.12 is enforced by convention plus fixtures, not by types. A second developer, or Fable six months later, can add a twenty-sixth construction that no test names. This is the real maintainability price of refusing a component library and it should be stated to the director rather than argued away.

The render kernel is code we own: ~150 lines of keyed patching and focus preservation with no community fixes behind it. A subtle bug there shows up as a wrong row identity during a live run, which is the worst place for it. It needs its own adversarial tests and it is the one piece of this option with no external validation.

Evolve does not settle information architecture. If K-02/K-20 lands on a two-axis model with content lanes, E2 and E3 do materially more work than sketched, and the screen-by-screen growth that makes evolve cheap becomes a series of partial IAs living side by side during the transition.

E4 depends on a writer assignment this option cannot make (CF-22) and on the independent review of a branch it may not patch. If the seam's review returns large changes, core/repo.mjs is written against a moving target.

The deferred-JSON-parse win is Inferred. If Firefox Android's JSON.parse of a 96 KB string is not materially cheaper than the object literal, the startup argument in q14 evaporates and only the size gate remains.

Nothing here is verified in a browser. Every claim about adoptedStyleSheets, reduced-motion reaching a userscript overlay, glyph coverage, navigator.storage.persist(), the legacy Builder FAB's position over the overlay, and touch-target behaviour at 360 px is Inferred and needs the user's smoke.

Builder is not retired by any of E0-E4. The seven hard blockers (B.3.1) are all in E5, so the option's first four slices improve the tool the operator uses least for the workflows that most often send them back to Builder. That ordering is defensible (safety seam first) but it is a real delay to the retirement the brief wants, and reordering E5 before E3 is a legitimate alternative the director may prefer.

q1.question: Evolve the current Forge UI in place vs replace the UI layer while preserving runner/storage/transport
q1.answer: Evolve in place, with one hard structural move first (E1) and no rewrite. Three pieces of evidence decide it. (a) The layer boundary already exists and is already correct: A_ARCHITECTURE_MAP.md A.2 marks every module below ui/ 'UI-independent: yes', and compose() (forge/src/main.mjs:35-57) is the seam a second host would consume; a replacement would be rebuilding the half that is not broken's consumer while keeping the half that is. (b) The actual defects are enumerable and small: ten blocks of domain logic in ui/app.mjs, one async-into-detached-tree pattern (screens.mjs:90-97,111-119 and the app.state._renderPicker back-channel at screens.mjs:92 read at app.mjs:194,204), one full-region re-render every 1500 ms (app.mjs:268), three sub-floor touch targets, and one outcome-vs-state colour bug (styles.mjs:44). None of those is a reason to discard 329 lines of screen code that encodes hard-won safety wording. (c) The approved visual direction has ALREADY been sequenced as an in-place evolution: D_VISUAL_SYSTEM.md D2.6 S1 says 'Runs on the existing five screens; forge/test/ui.test.mjs selectors keep working'. A replacement would discard that sequencing and its costing for no stated benefit. The cost of evolving, stated plainly: the accumulated hand-written markup stays hand-written, so the 25-component inventory in A.12 is enforced by convention plus committed fixtures rather than by a type system, and the unminified bundle grows about 24%.

q2.question: Do the vanilla DOM/CSSOM build constraints remain desirable, or can a component strategy improve maintainability without breaking userscript/takeover behaviour?
q2.answer: They remain required, and the maintainability gain comes from a 150-line render kernel rather than a library. Template-literal libraries (Lit, htm, uhtml) route through an HTML string sink, which forge/build.mjs fails the build on and forge/test/ui.test.mjs:29-34 greps for across all of src; adopting one means relaxing a shipped safety gate. A VDOM library without a string sink (Preact) would pass the gate but adds a dependency to an artefact that must be byte-reproducible for the release pin and self-contained for the single @require model, to buy diffing the kernel provides in 150 lines. Takeover is untouched either way: takeover.mjs does not care what renders inside .f-host. The real maintainability win is not a library but a boundary - screens stop reading `app` and take a plain view-model, which is what makes the 25 WCM components in A.12 buildable and testable without a second shell.

q3.question: How to keep the execution core UI-independent enough for future shell/native hosting
q3.answer: Move the ten domain blocks out of ui/app.mjs into forge/src/core/ (E1), give core an event emitter and a serialisable core.snapshot(), and make that snapshot the only thing screens read. A second host then needs exactly three things: call compose(), subscribe to core events, render core.snapshot(). Nothing in core imports from ui/; nothing in ui/ imports from runner/storage/transport except through core. The proof that the boundary is real is mechanical, not aspirational: core.snapshot() is JSON-serialisable, so it is committed as a CI fixture and diffed - if a screen needs something the snapshot does not carry, the fixture diff shows it. A.12's closing paragraph names exactly this list as 'the domain logic that ui/app.mjs owns ... the list a second shell or a native host would otherwise duplicate'.

q5.question: Storage migration and compatibility for existing journals, capture cache and settings
q5.answer: Three rules. (1) Do not move JOURNAL_VERSION for the first four phases; carry repository sync state in a separate tnr_forge_sync_v1 key. When a journal v2 becomes genuinely necessary, it is one additive step in the empty MIGRATIONS table (journal.mjs:407), and because migrate() refuses a record newer than the running bundle (journal.mjs:413) while rollback means reinstalling the previous pin, v2 may only be WRITTEN one release after the release that can READ it is pinned. (2) Repo text leaves the game read cache (app.mjs:198-200) for a SEPARATE database tnr_forge_repo v1, not a third store in tnr_forge - because an operator rolling back to a bundle that opens tnr_forge at v2 against an existing v3 gets VersionError and loses the capture snapshots with it. (3) tnr_bk_idmap_v1 and tnr_bk_gh_v1 are untouched for the whole roadmap because Builder v4.32 is still installed. A failed migration never deletes: it parks under <key>.corrupt as compat.mjs already does, and journal.broken finally gets a renderer.

q7.question: Procedure registry expansion and source-drift gates
q7.answer: Expansion is additive and stays a runner-layer change with its own review, never a side effect of UI work: rows transcribed from the pinned source with kind, limited and auth recorded explicitly, covered by auth.test.mjs's existing 'transcribed from source' invariant, and anything outside the registry still throws before any fetch. Which procedures may be added is user decision K-17 and retirement gate G-02 (combat.getBattleHistory, combat.getBattleEntries, gameAsset.getAllFolders are the proven real-work set). Drift gate: run the derive tools plus pin_relevance.mjs against the game head of the day as a phase-0 step of every implementation brief, and carry the pin SHA in the bundle banner and the Settings About card. The measured position today is that Forge is NOT blocked by drift - from 345d18ac to head 36c5873b the six field sets and nine nested families regenerate byte-identically and auth/kind/limiter are identical for all 43 registry paths - while the repository's own 45x set IS stale, which is a separate and higher-value re-extraction pass. Moving the Forge pin is K-13.

q11.question: Workstream integration and discovery
q11.answer: Read first, write only if ruled. core.repo.loadProject() projects state/workstreams/<slug>/roadmap.json through the same envelope as every other repository operation, and the Command Center shows the active workstream's ready and blocked tasks with their open_decisions. Validation and rendering stay in scripts/content_workstream.py - C.6 lists it among the things Forge may present, invoke or project but never reimplement, and the projections are generated, never hand-edited. Whether Forge may WRITE roadmap.json at all is K-28 and is not settled here. Discovery widens in two controlled steps: the package picker gains workstream-referenced manifest paths beside push/ on main (today it lists push/*.json only, app.mjs:186-207), and Studio build outputs become discoverable ONLY through the reviewed promotion contract (K-39), never by pointing the picker at studio/quest/<id> branches - that would be the copy-paste relay replaced by an unreviewed one.

q12.question: Result / harvest contract evolution
q12.answer: Evolve the bundle additively and gate every change on agreement with the real consumers. Three concrete changes. (1) Fix checks:null. A Forge bundle carries checks:null, validate.py --parity does set(bundle.get('checks',[])) and raises TypeError, and session_close.py --guards runs parity on the lexically newest inbox bundle - so every Forge run turns the content session's close guard red until a Builder bundle lands, which is a hidden pressure to keep Builder alive. The honest fix is to emit a real checks inventory from Forge's own validator and lints; the alternative (make parity skip cfg:'forge') hides the gap. This is a Builder retirement gate. (2) Add capture bodies on list reads under gate G-03, because 23 committed generator scripts read captures[].data and Forge summary captures carry none - that single omission is why answers/ is still fed only by Builder. (3) Add the sync state and keep state/outcome/forgeState/verdict/journal exactly as they are. Every change is gated by an agreement test: seven tests already shell out to the real harvest.py, and a validate.py --parity fixture joins them.

q13.question: Audit / history model
q13.answer: The journal stays the single record of truth for what was SENT and what the server confirmed; nothing competes with it. Added beside it: an append-only action log per job recording the human intents (which core intent, which confirmation tier, at what time, from which tab) so a bundle can answer 'who asked for this and what were they shown', which today only the journal's mechanical transitions can partially reconstruct. It is exported inside the results bundle and never replaces a journal entry. Three deliberate limits. (a) No second canon: the log records intents and renderings, not facts about live state (RUL-2026-09-12-002). (b) It is not an approval store - where admin approval state lives is K-09 and the game has no native approval field. (c) Publish actions get an audit entry with the dependency check and the read-back result once K-03/K-05/K-12 land (R-08), not before. The journal's own export (journal.exportText, journal.mjs:398-400) and journal.broken finally get a UI surface, which they do not have today.

q14.question: Bundle size, performance and startup on mobile
q14.answer: Measured this session: forge_bundle.js 397,984 B raw / 74,304 B gzip -9; src/ui sources 70,135 B raw / 21,498 B gzip (ratio 0.307); 65.9 source bytes per line across src/ui. Projection for this option: +46 KB for core and the kernel, +32 KB for screens and components, +16-20 KB CSS = about +95 KB raw and +29 KB gzip, i.e. ~493 KB raw / ~103 KB gzip unminified, or about 290 KB / 72 KB if K-14 authorises minify:true. So evolve GROWS the artefact by roughly a quarter and R-06 gets worse in bytes. The startup cost is a different and more tractable problem: the loader matches the whole origin, so the IIFE evaluates on every game page, and the three contract JSONs are embedded as top-level JavaScript object literals (forge_bundle.js:2802, :6245, :6658) totalling 124,782 source bytes that are parsed before boot() returns on an unarmed tab (main.mjs:171-173). Switching them to esbuild's text loader with a memoised JSON.parse moves that parse and its retained heap to first use - never on an INERT page. Same bytes on the wire. The size of the win on Firefox Android is Inferred; the embedding shape is source-verified. Guard: raw and gzip ceilings asserted per release, and the first smoke of each phase is measured on the user's actual device.
evidence: measured: wc -c and gzip -9 in this session

q15.question: Release / pin / install strategy
q15.answer: One bundle, one @require, one immutable pin - unchanged, and deliberately so: a second artefact is not covered by the pin, needs a second pin_release.py target, and breaks the offline-and-evicted recovery story. The two-stage pin (@x-release-pending then release_pin.yml rewriting @require to the merge commit) is unchanged. Phase 0 must have main green, which needs release_loader.test.mjs:47's 'exactly one marker' relaxed to 'at most one'; the only existing fix is bundled with unrelated loader-assertion rewrites on the ChatGPT branch, so this option authors no competing change and records the assignment as a prerequisite (CF-19, R-22). Two CI additions: raw+gzip size ceilings, and push/**/*.json in forge.yml's path filter, because runner.test.mjs and check_release_pin.mjs read those files and a manifest change can ship today without a forge run. Minification is recommended but is K-14 and must keep the bundle byte-reproducible on the pinned esbuild so the bundle-diff job keeps meaning something. Install for the operator is unchanged: ViolentMonkey refetch after each pin; the About card grows the pin SHA and the storage versions so a support question is answerable from the phone.
evidence: forge_loader_user.js:12 and its RELEASE PIN comment block

q16.question: Recovery after tab eviction, crash and network loss across the new UI
q16.answer: The rule is that the view-model is derived from durable sources, so a bigger UI adds no new volatile state. Eviction: only the selected manifest PATH is persisted, never the parsed plan, so a stale plan can never be run; capture snapshots stay immutable; navigator.storage.persist() moves into core.health so every surface renders one answer (its outcome on Firefox Android is still Inferred). Crash mid-run: completely unchanged - withSent flushes SENT before the fetch (journal.mjs:330-335), run() refuses a job with SENT items and resume() reconciles first; the new progress event is advisory and an adversarial test proves it cannot advance an item state; and no control anywhere gains a Retry label for a mutation class. Network loss: a new sync state with retry-on-demand, never an automatic retry loop, because the repository automation already uses rebase-and-retry on disjoint paths. And the one Behaviour-proven recovery defect gets fixed: showExport prepends the results card to $main (app.mjs:182) and _drive's finally calls refresh() which replaces $main (app.mjs:299), so with sync off the operator's only copy of the bundle is destroyed by the next render. Under a view-model the pending export is state, so it survives; a regression test asserts it survives three re-renders.

q18.question: Test architecture for a much larger UI and capability surface
q18.answer: Four socket-free layers plus one user-owned browser smoke. (1) Unit: the core facades become plain functions, so harvestEntry, _materialize, blockedPaths and exportJob - today reachable only through a mounted App - are unit-testable with no DOM; all 75 adversarial, 45 auth, 19 journal and 16 budget cases stay untouched, and 'not one of them was edited' is E1's diff gate. (2) Contract/fixture: committed core.snapshot() fixtures per scenario, diffed in CI exactly as the 11 recorded tRPC envelope fixtures already are; new github.mjs and upload.mjs fixtures, since both are on the write path and have zero tests today; a validate.py --parity agreement case beside the seven tests that already shell out to the real harvest.py. (3) UI-contract: a deterministic DOM serializer over .f-app producing one committed snapshot per screen x machine state, with the state list enumerated from the journal's TRANSITIONS table so a state cannot exist without a rendered fixture; plus axe-core and KeyboardEvent dispatch in jsdom; plus the stylesheet scoping and contrast contract test; plus the 13 semantic guarantees mapped one-to-one to named tests, of which only five are covered today. (4) Adversarial additions: no rendered control can reach a send path while an item is SENT, asserted by walking handlers against a core allow-list rather than by reading markup; no progress event can change an item state; a DONE job with outcome 'unverified' never renders the success construction; every durable-class notice has a persistent surface; the export card survives re-render. (5) The browser smoke stays user-owned, read-only first, and enumerated as a checklist; Playwright or any real-browser CI layer needs a user ruling against the socket-free rule and is not in these phases.

weaknesses: Evolve does not shrink the bundle. Unminified it grows about 24% (measured base 397,984 B raw / 74,304 B gzip; projected ~493 KB / ~103 KB), which makes R-06 worse in bytes on a phone. The only genuine byte relief is minify:true, which is user decision K-14, and the JSON-parse deferral saves parse time and heap, not bytes.

E1 is the classic silent-behaviour-change phase: 'move ten blocks, change nothing' is exactly where a wording or an ordering quietly shifts. The mitigation is mechanical (E0 commits the DOM snapshots; E1 must leave them byte-identical) but the mitigation only works if E0 actually lands first, unedited.

Keeping hand-written h() markup means the 25-component inventory in A.12 is enforced by convention plus fixtures, not by types. A second developer, or Fable six months later, can add a twenty-sixth construction that no test names. This is the real maintainability price of refusing a component library and it should be stated to the director rather than argued away.

The render kernel is code we own: ~150 lines of keyed patching and focus preservation with no community fixes behind it. A subtle bug there shows up as a wrong row identity during a live run, which is the worst place for it. It needs its own adversarial tests and it is the one piece of this option with no external validation.

Evolve does not settle information architecture. If K-02/K-20 lands on a two-axis model with content lanes, E2 and E3 do materially more work than sketched, and the screen-by-screen growth that makes evolve cheap becomes a series of partial IAs living side by side during the transition.

E4 depends on a writer assignment this option cannot make (CF-22) and on the independent review of a branch it may not patch. If the seam's review returns large changes, core/repo.mjs is written against a moving target.

The deferred-JSON-parse win is Inferred. If Firefox Android's JSON.parse of a 96 KB string is not materially cheaper than the object literal, the startup argument in q14 evaporates and only the size gate remains.

Nothing here is verified in a browser. Every claim about adoptedStyleSheets, reduced-motion reaching a userscript overlay, glyph coverage, navigator.storage.persist(), the legacy Builder FAB's position over the overlay, and touch-target behaviour at 360 px is Inferred and needs the user's smoke.

Builder is not retired by any of E0-E4. The seven hard blockers (B.3.1) are all in E5, so the option's first four slices improve the tool the operator uses least for the workflows that most often send them back to Builder. That ordering is defensible (safety seam first) but it is a real delay to the retirement the brief wants, and reordering E5 before E3 is a legitimate alternative the director may prefer.
